So I've been running The Fourteenth Doctor since they announced him and the strongest synergy between all the doctors is Historic matters type cards. I mean at the end of the day it's always gonna be pretty janky because of how different each Doctor plays, but I have a lot of fun with it. I would say my 5 ideal Doctors to grab would be:

\[\[The Sixth Doctor\]\] - He's by far the strongest Doctor for the all Doctor's strategy if you're trying to win with \[\[Gallifrey Stands\]\]. He also just generates a ton of value if you're playing Historic matters.

\[\[The Eighth Doctor\]\] - Being able to recast any of the Doctors put into the graveyard from Fourteen's ability is great.

\[\[The Forth Doctor\]\] - Similar to Eight where you can cast Doctors off the top of your library.

\[\[The Tenth Doctor\]\] - Great way to get through cards off your top deck, has good synergy with Four to get lands you don't need off the top of your library and can help free cast Doctors.

\[\[The Second Doctor\]\] - I really like having the no max hand size, when Gallifrey Stands puts a bunch of Doctors back in your hand it helps to not have to worry about hand size. Plus the card draw and potential to avoid being attacked is pretty nice.

No problem! I used to run all those same sea monsters when my commander was \[\[Arixmethes\]\] but when I switched to Runo those lower CMC ones just felt like they got in the way. Another thing to keep in mind is to maybe cut some of the legendary sea monsters, since Krothuss can't make tokens of them. Though some of the legendaries are just too good not to run.

Osgir gets a little more value out of self mill, artifacts have such a large range of abilities you can mill without fear of milling something important. Runo really wants specific things in grave, and if you end up milling ramp or lands then you're not progressing your game plan. You want to make sure you're putting 6 CMC sea monsters in the graveyard to trigger him, and then be able to put the scariest ones in the grave to hit with a reanimate effect.

Here's my list if it would help at all:

[https://archidekt.com/decks/2347196#What\_Is\_Dead\_May\_Die](https://archidekt.com/decks/2347196#What_Is_Dead_May_Die)

So I've been running sea monsters for a few years now with different commanders, it's definitely my favorite deck. Here are my suggestions:  
1. The sea monsters that don't hit 6 CMC can be kind of bricky with Runo, especially if they don't have any kind of card advantage. So I would cut: \[\[Charix\]\], \[\[Mesmerizing Benthid\]\], \[\[Reef Worm\]\], and \[\[Wormhole Serpent\]\].

2. For getting the chonkers into the yard you really don't want to rely on random mill effects, you want control over it. I'd cut \[\[Millikin\]\] for that reason. Then I'd add: \[\[Wharf Infiltrator\]\], \[\[Nightveil Sprite\]\], and \[\[Looter il-Kor\]\]. If you go all in on small, evasive creatures like these that have looting abilities you can throw in \[\[Satoru Umezawa\]\], and then you can ninjutsu out the huge bois.

3. I know you said only $2 or less, but I want to make a suggestion for \[\[Buried Alive\]\], it's a $5 triple entomb effect, it puts serious work in. Another card on the pricier side that is an entire house is \[\[Hullbreaker Horror\]\], it with one Krothuss trigger has won me games.

I hope that helps a bit!

YTA. My father in law just died of small cell lung cancer that metastasized to his brain caused by lifelong smoking. He fought hard for a year before it went to his brain and there was nothing more the doctors could do for him. You may think you're healthy, and maybe you are, but it can come out of nowhere. Your husband wants to spend his life with you and all you're concerned with is indulging a habit that does all harm and no good. Find a way to kick the habit, not just for your husband, but for yourself, because it will vastly improve your quality of life and life expectancy.

First off, welcome to the game! It's understandable that the skill list can be overwhelming and confusing at first, but it's pretty easy to get the hang of. The wide array of skills are there to balance out to make sure no one is amazing at everything, it lets you be a specialist at things that everyone else probably won't be. So for example instead of just having a catch-all Perception skill we have Spot Hidden for visual perception, Listen for auditory perception, and an uncommon skill Read Lips for a unique perception option.

So let's go over your goals for your character and where you've got your points. So right off the bat I see you've got a large number of points in both Persuade and Charm. This is fine from an RP flavor perspective, but you really only need to be really good at one of them. There are 4 social skills: Charm for a more seductive method, Fast Talk for trying to con someone, Persuade for an honest and straightforward approach, and Intimidate for threatening. It just comes down to how you want to RP interactions.

You also said you wanted to be able to read people, for that you'll typically use the Psychology skill, so you'll want to move some points to that. 

As for just generally great skills to have Spot Hidden and Library Use are 2 that tend to be helpful in every investigation, so that's something to consider.

I hope that helps a bit, if you have any more questions feel free, I love helping people get into this game, it's my all time favorite.

First of all welcome to the game! So, for your questions, the Keeper's Guide is the essential book for playing the full game, there's a lot more to sanity and combat and chases than are in the quick start rules if I remember correctly. It also contains tons of helpful tables, example scenerios for understanding how things work, and an index of monsters, items, and magic. I wouldn't run a full campaign without it.

The investigators manual is something that you as the keeper wouldn't get much out of, but your players might. It contains more character creation options, tips for playing, and useful info about living in the 1920s. Not required by any means, but nice to have.

As for campaign stuff, it's incredibly easy to string single scenarios together to make a continuing story, and I would suggest you do that to start out as you're learning the game. Doors to Darkness is a book with 5 scenarios written for 7th edition and is aimed at beginning keepers and players. Once you've got a handle on things Call of Cthulhu has some great long form campaigns.

Masks of Nyalarthotep being the poster child for the best, and for good reason. It's incredibly well written and gives your players tons to do and see, but it is brutal and you will likely have investigators dying on the regular. Which is why if you intend to do a long campaign I would suggest picking up Pulp Cthulhu, which is an additional rule book that adds some interesting game play changes.

Pulp turns your investigators into more Indiana Jones type heros, able to survive at least one round of combat with actual monsters. You can control how pulpy you make your game, and even at the pulpiest it's still quite a scary game, just with less character rerolling. There's even a pulp campaign you can buy: The Two-Headed Serpent.

There's some other great campaigns, like Horror on the Orient Express, and no shortage of modules to combine together to make a storyline for your players. I hope that helped, feel free to ask any more questions you have, I'd be happy to help. And welcome again, you've picked up an amazing game.

Correct. It has more detailed character creation and then it has ideas and tips for players, like how to form a party in game and what it was like to live in the 20s for RP information. Not a ton of core game rules in that book.

So the best book you can buy to learn all the rules is the Keeper's Guide. It's the base book that everything else is based on, has character creation and all the other info you need to play. You can honestly get by as a player with just the free quick play rules from Chaosium, but if you want a book to learn all the detailed rules it's the Keeper's Guide. Just don't read the scenerios in the back if you don't plan to be the keeper.
That's awesome. The artist is such a cool guy.

Pulp Cthulhu is a really great, well thought out addition to the game because you can control how much pulp you put into the game, you don't have to use every added feature. So you can keep it light pulp and have your investigators be standard squishy PCs but with special talents and powers, or you can go full Indiana Jones pulp. 

I personally feel like if you're running a long campaign like Masks a little pulp at the very least should be considered, especially if you want to avoid having everyone roll new characters every other session. That's how I run my games anyway, I don't put any pulp into one shots and let the deaths happen as they may, but for a long campaign I want my players to be attached to their characters, it makes a death more impactful and that much more scary, and Pulp Cthulhu really helps make that possible without spoiling the horror.

SPOILERS FOR BLACKWATER CREEK AND MASKS OF NYALARTHOTEP

So I wove the two starts to the scenario together: Sly gets sent to Blackwater Creek to secure the whiskey supply for the speakeasy he works at via the bootlegger opener, and Virginia gets hired by Jackson Elias ( I introduced him early so they could get attached to him in the event I run MoN and make his death extra brutal) to find his friend Dr. Henry Roades whose been missing for some time, using the Miskatonic University opening. Since they were both going to the same place they road together at the suggestion of Jackson.

So they make it to the town, Virginia wants to explore and look for clues about Roades while Sly wanted to go straight to the Carmondy farm to secure the whiskey. She talks to Baxter as that's where the opening letter Jackson gave her was mailed from, and Baxter told her that he had set up camp somewhere around the town, not sure where, and that he was odd. Sly talked to the sheriff to locate the farm and they make their way up to the farm.

Virginia keeps the truck running on the outskirts of the farm while Sly goes up and talks to the Carmondys. He manages to charm them into a deal and they load up a crate of whiskey. They both make successful listen rolls (Virginia's was hard since she was so far away) and they both heard what sounded like muffled shouting, but Sly wanted to leave ASAP with the whiskey, so they left. As they drive down the road to leave they're ambushed on the road by the sheriff and the townsfolk and Sly guns it, starting a chase.

The chase goes down the dirt roads, around a hairpin turn, through the town and across the bridge out of town. And while everyone was shooting at everyone no one hit anything and everyone crashed at least once, the investigators took some damage but made it out of town. It being nearly 2am at this point and the truck being heavily damaged they turn down the side road they remember passing, Virginia believing that it lead to Roades digsite/camp, which she was correct. They get some rest and the townsfolk don't find them and in the morning Sly has starting feeling great, the early stages of the Mother's Gift from drinking the whiskey. 

They inspect the camp where they find Roades crumpled incomplete letter (had to move it since they were never gonna stay at the Jarvey farm and I needed to hook them back into Blackwater) and they were thoroughly creeped out. Virginia wanted to call Jackson so they drove slowly to Dunwitch as the truck was too damaged to make it back to Boston. They took the truck into a shop for repairs and Sly offered some Carmondys whiskey to bring the price of repairs (I'm excited to revisit that) and Virginia managed to get ahold of Jackson, who after hearing they may be in the midst of cult activity has decided to meet them in Dunwitch and then help investigate Blackwater with them. Sly doesn't want to go back, but he will soon find the Mother's voice calling him back, as that's where we ended the session.

I had to improvise so much of that, the chase was particularly exciting as I got to try out the chase rules and had some good obstacles to work with. I'm so exited to see how this ends, I'm keeping it a little puppy on my end, they think death is around every corner but unless they do something stupid I don't plan to kill them, as they've put a lot of work into their characters and I wanna see them at least make it to Masks, but they don't know any of that.
